claims.text: Post-processing additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components with deep cryogenic treatment reduces fabrication-induced defects.
Deep cryogenic treatment improves the dimensional precision of additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components relative to the as-deposited state.
Deep cryogenic treatment enhances the mechanical integrity of additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components relative to the as-deposited state.
As-deposited laser-melted Hf-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr components contain microstructural defects.
As-deposited laser-melted Hf-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr components contain residual stresses.
As-deposited laser-melted Hf-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr components have moderate dimensional imprecision.
Deep cryogenic treatment can be applied to laser-melting-deposited Hf-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy without additional mechanical deformation.
Deep cryogenic treatment relieves residual stresses in the additively manufactured alloy.
Deep cryogenic treatment refines the alloy microstructure and grain boundaries.
Deep cryogenic treatment induces a phase transition in laser-melting-deposited Hf0.25NbTa0.25TiZr alloy without additional deformation.
Cryogenic contraction is the mechanism by which deep cryogenic treatment relieves residual stress and refines the microstructure.
Deep cryogenic treatment diminishes internal voids and other defects formed during rapid solidification.
The proposed microstructural changes improve dimensional stability.
The proposed microstructural changes increase both strength and ductility.
In laser-melting-deposited Hf0.25NbTa0.25TiZr, deep cryogenic treatment increases tensile strength by 11% and elongation by 10% relative to the as-deposited alloy.
Prior results show strength improvements up to 25% and ductility improvements of 10–48% following deep cryogenic treatment.
Hf-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr high-entropy alloys treated in the cited work have a BCC structure.
The intervention should generalize to similar single-phase BCC high-entropy alloys fabricated by laser additive manufacturing.
The direct effect of deep cryogenic treatment on dimensional precision has not been quantitatively established by the cited evidence.
